|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090720195141/http://www.variety.com/article/VR1118006123.html?categoryid=14&cs=1 |archive-date=July 20, 2009}}</ref> The situation was later resolved, and the entire original voice-cast returned for the new episodes.

Near the end of a message from Maurice LaMarche sent to members of the "Save the Voices of Futurama" group on Facebook, LaMarche announced that the original cast would be returning for the new episodes.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 31, 2009 |title=Save the Voices of Futurama |url=https://www.facebook.com/home.php#/group.php?gid=216285555057 |url-status=live |access-date=July 31, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140720191115/https://www.facebook.com/home.php#/group.php?gid=216285555057 |archive-date=July 20, 2014}}</ref> The ''[[Toronto Star]]'' confirmed, announcing on their website that the original cast of ''Futurama'' signed contracts with Fox to return for 26 more episodes.<ref>Salem, Rob. [https://www.thestar.com/comment/columnists/article/674841 "Futurama cast members ink new deal with Fox"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130121041504/http://www.thestar.com/comment/columnists/article/674841 |date=January 21, 2013}}, ''Toronto Star'', July 31, 2009</ref> Similarly, an email sent to fans from Cohen and Groening reported that West, Sagal, DiMaggio, LaMarche, MacNeille, Tom, LaMarr, and Herman would all be returning for the revival.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Frucci |first=Adam |date=August 25, 2009 |title=Futurama Returning with Full Original Cast After All |url=https://gizmodo.com/5345037/futurama-returning-with-full-original-cast-after-all |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090828001239/http://gizmodo.com/5345037/futurama-returning-with-full-original-cast-after-all |archive-date=August 28, 2009 |access-date=August 25, 2009 |publisher=[[Gizmodo]]}}</ref>

Cohen told ''[[Newsday]]'' in August 2009 that the reported 26-episode order means "[i]t will be up to 26. I can't guarantee it will be 26. But I think there's a pretty good chance it'll be exactly 26. Fox has been a little bit cagey about it, even internally. But nobody's too concerned. We're plunging ahead".<ref name="newsday">[[Frank Lovece|Lovece, Frank]]. [http://www.newsday.com/entertainment/tv/futurama-finds-a-new-future-on-comedy-central-1.1402526 "'Futurama' finds a new future on Comedy Central"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090831180647/http://www.newsday.com/entertainment/tv/futurama-finds-a-new-future-on-comedy-central-1.1402526 |date=August 31, 2009}}, ''[[Newsday]]'', August 28, 2009; posted online August 27, 2009</ref> Two episodes were in the process of being voice-recorded at that time, with an additional "six scripts ... in the works, ranging in scale from 'it's a crazy idea that someone's grandmother thought of' to 'it's all on paper'.<ref name="newsday" />

When ''Futurama'' aired June 24, 2010, on Comedy Central, it helped the network to its highest-rated night in 2010 and its highest-rated Thursday primetime in the network's history.<ref name="Gough">{{Cite web |last=Gough |first=Paul J. |date=June 29, 2010 |title="Futurama" returns with strong ratings |url=https://news.yahoo.com/s/nm/20100629/tv_nm/us_futurama |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100711180204/https://news.yahoo.com/s/nm/20100629/tv_nm/us_futurama <!--Added by H3llBot--> |archive-date=July 11, 2010 |access-date=July 1, 2010 |publisher=[[Yahoo! News]]}}</ref> In March 2011, it was announced that ''Futurama'' had been renewed for a seventh season, consisting of at least 26 episodes, scheduled to air in 2012 and 2013.<ref name="Renewal">{{Cite magazine |last=Hibberd |first=James |date=March 24, 2011 |title='Futurama' Renewed for Two More Years! |url=https://ew.com/article/2011/03/24/futurama-renewed/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110328090316/http://insidetv.ew.com/2011/03/24/futurama-renewed/ |archive-date=March 28, 2011 |access-date=February 9, 2022 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]}}</ref><ref name="CCSeason7announcement">{{Cite web |date=March 29, 2011 |title=Comedy Central® Renews "Futurama" for 26 New Episodes |url=https://press.cc.com/press-release/2011/03/28/032811_futurama-renewed-for-26-new-episodes |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110405101048/http://www.comedycentral.com/press/press_releases/2011/032811_futurama-renewed-for-26-new-episodes.jhtml |archive-date=April 5, 2011 |access-date=February 9, 2022 |website=Comedy Central Press Release}}</ref> The first episode of season 7 premiered June 20, 2012, on Comedy Central.<ref name="StartSeason7A">[http://www.comedycentral.com/shows/futurama Futurama – Series | Comedy Central Official Site | ComedyCentral.com] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319151858/http://www.comedycentral.com/shows/futurama |date=March 19, 2012}}, ''[[Comedy Central]]''. Retrieved March 27, 2012</ref>

Due to the uncertain future of the series, there have been four designated [[series finale]]s.<ref name="canceled">{{Cite news |last=Itzkoff |first=Dave |date=April 22, 2013 |title=Comedy Central Cancels 'Futurama' |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=http://artsbeat.blogs.nytimes.com/2013/04/22/comedy-central-cancels-futurama |url-status=live |access-date=April 22, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141206182520/http://artsbeat.blogs.nytimes.com/2013/04/22/comedy-central-cancels-futurama/ |archive-date=December 6, 2014}}</ref> "[[The Devil's Hands Are Idle Playthings]]", ''[[Futurama: Into the Wild Green Yonder|Into the Wild Green Yonder]]'', "[[Overclockwise]]", and "[[Meanwhile (Futurama)|Meanwhile]]" have all been written to serve as a final episode for the show.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cortez, Carl |date=September 1, 2010 |title=Exclusive Interview: 'FUTURAMA' CO-CREATOR DAVID X. COHEN BLOWS OUT THE 100TH EPISODE CANDLE AND TALKS ABOUT THE SEASON SIX FINALE |url=http://ifmagazine.com/feature.asp?article=3955 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100907171942/http://ifmagazine.com/feature.asp?article=3955 |archive-date=September 7, 2010 |access-date=March 19, 2012 |website=If}}</ref><ref name="Exclusive Page 3">{{Cite web |last=Zalben, Alex |date=June 22, 2010 |title=Exclusive: Futurama Creator Spills on Special Last, Last Episode! (Page 3) |url=http://www.ugo.com/tv/futurama-david-x-cohen-interview?page=3 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615043537/http://www.ugo.com/tv/futurama-david-x-cohen-interview?page=3 |archive-date=June 15, 2011 |access-date=August 25, 2010 |website=UGO}}</ref>

===Comedy Central cancellation===
Comedy Central announced in April 2013 that they would be airing the then final episode "[[Meanwhile (Futurama)|Meanwhile]]" on September 4, 2013.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Marechal |first=AJ |title=Toon comedy has logged seasons on Fox, Comedy Central since 1999 |work=Variety |url=https://variety.com/2013/tv/news/futurama-cancelled-by-comedy-central-1200406963/ |url-status=live |access-date=April 22, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130424030528/http://variety.com/2013/tv/news/futurama-cancelled-by-comedy-central-1200406963/ |archive-date=April 24, 2013}}</ref> The producers said that they are exploring options for the future of the series as "[they] have many more stories to tell", but would gauge fan reaction to the news.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dan Snierson |date=April 22, 2013 |title='Futurama' to end seven-season run on Sept. 4 – EXCLUSIVE |url=http://insidetv.ew.com/2013/04/22/futurama-not-renewed-comedy-central/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130422150351/http://insidetv.ew.com/2013/04/22/futurama-not-renewed-comedy-central/ |archive-date=April 22, 2013 |access-date=April 22, 2013 |website=Inside TV}}</ref> Groening and Cohen had previously expressed a desire to produce a theatrical film or another [[direct-to-video]] film upon conclusion of the series.<ref name="IGNFuturama">{{Cite web |last=Max Nicholson |date=April 23, 2013 |title=Futurama's Back, and Bigger Than the Red Hot Chili Peppers! |url=https://uk.ign.com/articles/2012/06/18/futuramas-back-and-bigger-than-the-red-hot-chili-peppers?page=2 |access-date=April 23, 2013 |publisher=IGN}}</ref>

In an August 2013 interview with ''[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]'', [[Katey Sagal]] said regarding the series finale, "So I don't believe it... I just hold out hope for it because it has such a huge fan base, it's such a smart show, and why wouldn't somebody want to keep making that show; so that's my thought, I'm just in denial that it's over". Sagal also mentioned during the same interview that Groening told her at [[San Diego Comic-Con International|Comic-Con]] that "we'll find a place" and "don't worry, it's not going to end".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Levy |first=Piet |date=September 1, 2013 |title=Video: Katey Sagal talks about 'Sons of Anarchy', 'Futurama,' Bob Dylan |url=http://www.jsonline.com/blogs/business/221993931.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130903153109/http://www.jsonline.com/blogs/business/221993931.html |archive-date=September 3, 2013 |access-date=September 6, 2013 |publisher=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]] |type=Interview}}</ref>

===''Simpsorama''===
''The Simpsons'' episode "[[Simpsorama]]" is an official [[Fictional crossover|crossover]] with ''Futurama''. It originally aired during the [[The Simpsons season 26|twenty-sixth season]] of ''The Simpsons'' on Fox on November 9, 2014, over a year after the ''Futurama'' series finale aired on Comedy Central.<ref>{{Cite magazine |title='The Simpsons' to join forces with 'Futurama' for crossover episode |url=http://insidetv.ew.com/2013/07/20/the-simpsons-futurama-crossover-epsidoe/ |url-status=dead|magazine=Entertainment Weekly |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130721032141/http://insidetv.ew.com/2013/07/20/the-simpsons-futurama-crossover-epsidoe/ |archive-date=July 21, 2013 |access-date=July 21, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite tweet |number=380740786121220096 |user=TheJohnDiMaggio |title=This is happening. Today is a good day. |author=John DiMaggio |date=September 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Under Construction sunnewsnetwork.ca |url=http://www.sunnewsnetwork.ca/sunnews/entertainment/archives/2013/09/20130928-084628.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131002020911/http://www.sunnewsnetwork.ca/sunnews/entertainment/archives/2013/09/20130928-084628.html |archive-date=October 2, 2013 |website=sunnewsnetwork.ca}}</ref>

=== Syndication ===
In July 2011, it was reported that the show had been picked up for [[Broadcast syndication|syndication]] by both local [[Network affiliate|affiliates]] and [[WGN America]]. Broadcast of old episodes began in September 2011.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=July 26, 2011 |title=WGN America Fall 2011 Schedule; MeTV Network Celebrates Lucille Ball's 100th Birthday With 100 Episodes of Lucy Series |url=http://blog.sitcomsonline.com/2011/07/wgn-america-fall-2011-schedule-metv.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110827124549/http://blog.sitcomsonline.com/2011/07/wgn-america-fall-2011-schedule-metv.html |archive-date=August 27, 2011 |access-date=August 23, 2011 |publisher=Blog.sitcomsonline.com}}</ref> On September 19, 2011, WGN America began re-running ''Futurama'', carrying it until 2014.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=October 19, 2011 |title=Futurama |url=http://www.wgnamerica.com/shows/futurama |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130209112538/http://www.wgnamerica.com/shows/futurama |archive-date=February 9, 2013 |access-date=November 1, 2011 |publisher=wgnamerica}}</ref> ''Futurama'' doubled its viewership in syndication in 2012.<ref name=":3">{{Cite tweet |number=164409657446764544 |user=EricRogersLA |title=#futurama doubles viewership in... |date=January 31, 2012 |access-date=January 31, 2012}}</ref>

In October 2017, [[Syfy]] announced that they had acquired syndication rights to all 140 episodes of ''Futurama'', adding it to its lineup on November 11, 2017, with a weekend long marathon.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Andreeva |first1=Nellie |last2=Petski |first2=Denise |date=October 3, 2017 |title=Syfy Acquires Matt Groening's 'Futurama' Animated Series |url=https://deadline.com/2017/10/syfy-acquires-matt-groening-futurama-animated-series-1202181103/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220219032550/https://deadline.com/2017/10/syfy-acquires-matt-groening-futurama-animated-series-1202181103/ |archive-date=February 19, 2022 |access-date=September 21, 2024 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]]}}</ref> ''Futurama'' was Syfy's first American animated series (the network had an [[anime]] programming block in the past), and eventually became paired with Syfy's TZGZ block of animated original series on Saturday nights. Comedy Central continued to air the series concurrently with Syfy, usually in the mornings and early afternoon. Syfy aired episodes from the first four seasons cropped to [[16:9 aspect ratio|16:9]] instead of airing them in their original [[Fullscreen (aspect ratio)|4:3]] aspect ratio; Comedy Central (since 2017) and FXX would do the same.

In September 2021, [[FXX]], which already carries ''The Simpsons'' and other 20th Television animated programming, announced that it would begin airing ''Futurama'' that November.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=September 17, 2021 |title=FXX Expands 'Family Guy' Rights To Full Catalog Of Past Seasons, Adds 'Futurama' Library |url=https://deadline.com/2021/09/family-guys-full-catalog-past-seasons-fxx-futurama-freeform-1234838887/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220219032555/https://deadline.com/2021/09/family-guys-full-catalog-past-seasons-fxx-futurama-freeform-1234838887/ |archive-date=February 19, 2022 |access-date=February 19, 2022 |website=Deadline}}</ref> Syfy stopped airing the show on November 10, 2021, and FXX began airing the show on November 15, 2021. Adult Swim then picked the show back up on December 27, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 13, 2021 |title=REPORT: Futurama Returns to Adult Swim This Month |url=https://www.cbr.com/report-futurama-returns-to-adult-swim-this-month/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211213030014/https://www.cbr.com/report-futurama-returns-to-adult-swim-this-month/ |archive-date=December 13, 2021 |access-date=December 13, 2021 |website=CBR}}</ref> Unlike FXX, Adult Swim airs the first four seasons in their original 4:3 aspect ratio, [[pillarbox]]ed. However, seasons 5 through 7, which were produced in 16:9, are cropped to 4:3. Comedy Central held the rights to the series, usually airing it in the early morning, but was since dropped as of September 19, 2025, with ''[[The Cleveland Show]]'' aired in its place at the begin and then later by ''[[South Park]]'',<ref>{{Cite web |title=TV Schedule for Comedy Central (US) – Eastern Feed |url=https://www.tvpassport.com/tv-listings/stations/comedy-central-us-eastern-feed/647/2022-05-02 |access-date=May 2, 2022 |website=TV Passport}}</ref> while Adult Swim dropped the show of the lineup as well after December 27, 2025, remaining on FXX in exclusive on the meantime.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.adultswim.com/schedule/|title=Adult Swim Schedule|website=[[Adult Swim]]|access-date=December 26, 2025}}</ref>

===Hulu revival===
In February 2022, Hulu revived the series with a 20-episode order to premiere in 2023. At the time of the announcement, the majority of the main voice cast was set to return, while John DiMaggio was still in negotiations.<ref name="hulurevival">{{Cite web |last=Goldberg |first=Lesley |date=February 9, 2022 |title='Futurama' Revived at Hulu |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/futurama-revived-at-hulu-1235090020/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220520035305/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/futurama-revived-at-hulu-1235090020/ |archive-date=May 20, 2022 |access-date=February 9, 2022 |website=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref> The next day, [[Disney+]] (Hulu's partner streaming service) announced in a press release that the new season would stream internationally as a Star Original.<ref>{{Cite web |title="Futurama" Lands Future at Disney+ with New Episodes |url=https://press.disney.co.uk/news/-futurama-lands-future-at-disney+-with-new-episodes}}</ref> DiMaggio stated that he had not accepted the role in mid-February 2022 because he believed the entire cast of ''Futurama'' should be paid more. He stated, "Bender is part of my soul and nothing about this is meant to be disrespectful to the fans or my ''Futurama'' family. It's about self-respect. And honestly, [it's about] being tired of an industry that's become far too corporate and takes advantage of artists' time and talent... I wish I could give you every detail so you would understand, but it's not my place."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Murphy |first=J. Kim |date=February 15, 2022 |title='Futurama' Voice Actor John DiMaggio Wants Entire Cast to Be Paid More for Revival: 'It's About Self-Respect' |url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/futurama-revival-bender-voice-actor-john-dimaggio-1235183272/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220216215215/https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/futurama-revival-bender-voice-actor-john-dimaggio-1235183272/ |archive-date=February 16, 2022 |access-date=February 18, 2022 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref>

In March, DiMaggio officially rejoined the series after working out a new deal, calling the prior events "Bendergate".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=March 1, 2022 |title=John DiMaggio To Return For 'Futurama' Revival On Hulu: "#Bendergate Is Officially Over" |url=https://deadline.com/2022/03/john-dimaggio-return-futurama-revival-hulu-bendergate-1234968435/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220524005212/https://deadline.com/2022/03/john-dimaggio-return-futurama-revival-hulu-bendergate-1234968435/ |archive-date=May 24, 2022 |access-date=March 1, 2022 |website=Deadline}}</ref> He later revealed that he did not get a raise, "but what I did get was a lot of respect". Had he not returned, Bender would have been voiced by a different guest star in each episode.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ettenhofer |first=Valerie |date=May 29, 2022 |title=Bender Voice Actor John DiMaggio 'Didn't Get More Money' After Futurama Contract Standoff |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/878158/bender-voice-actor-john-dimaggio-didnt-get-more-money-after-futurama-contract-standoff/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220528211448/https://www.slashfilm.com/878158/bender-voice-actor-john-dimaggio-didnt-get-more-money-after-futurama-contract-standoff/ |archive-date=May 28, 2022 |access-date=May 29, 2022 |website=Slash Film}}</ref> In August 2022, the titles of the first ten episodes were announced by Hulu,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lamadrid |first=Amanda |date=August 25, 2022 |title=Futurama Reboot Episode Titles Confirmed |url=https://screenrant.com/futurama-reboot-episode-titles-details/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220831131347/https://screenrant.com/futurama-reboot-episode-titles-details/ |archive-date=August 31, 2022 |access-date=August 31, 2022 |website=[[Screen Rant]]}}</ref> and by November 2022, the production team was aiming to complete the episodes by the end of the year.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Aguirre |first=Summer |date=November 3, 2022 |title=Young Pasadena artist talks joining 'Futurama' reboot team |url=https://www.pasadenaweekly.com/arts_and_events/young-pasadena-artist-talks-joining-futurama-reboot-team/article_02f68522-5ae8-11ed-b7ff-afbb7e1aa1c3.html |url-status=live |journal=[[Pasadena Weekly]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230112162729/https://www.pasadenaweekly.com/arts_and_events/young-pasadena-artist-talks-joining-futurama-reboot-team/article_02f68522-5ae8-11ed-b7ff-afbb7e1aa1c3.html |archive-date=January 12, 2023 |access-date=January 12, 2023}}</ref> In February 2023, a new release date was set sometime around the 2023 summer season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kesh |first=Jonathan |date=February 1, 2023 |title=Futurama's Revival Gets an Optimistic Release Window |url=https://www.cbr.com/futurama-revival-optimistic-release-window/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230203060023/https://www.cbr.com/futurama-revival-optimistic-release-window/ |archive-date=February 3, 2023 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=[[Comic Book Resources]]}}</ref> On May 18, 2023, a teaser trailer was released, announcing the premiere date as July 24, 2023.<ref name="teaser">{{Cite web |last=Otterson |first=Joe |date=May 18, 2023 |title='Futurama' Revival at Hulu Sets Premiere Date, Drops First Teaser |url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/news/futurama-revival-hulu-premiere-date-1235616847/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230518171244/https://variety.com/2023/tv/news/futurama-revival-hulu-premiere-date-1235616847/ |archive-date=May 18, 2023 |access-date=May 18, 2023 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref> This second revival has alternatively been titled the [[Futurama season 8|eighth]] and [[Futurama season 9|ninth]] seasons (production)<ref name="s8 trailer"/> and the eleventh and twelfth seasons (broadcast).<ref name="collider reboot"/><ref name="1101Synopsis" /> With the revival on Hulu, the season carries a new version of the opening title sequence, containing a briefly altered name "Hulurama" before reverting to "Futurama".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson Chapman |date=24 July 2023 |title=Hulu's 'Futurama' Revival Is Stuck in the Present |url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/commentary/futurama-review-hulu-reboot-too-topical-1234884831/ |publisher=Indie Web}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=18 May 2023 |title='Futurama' Returns July 24 on Hulu |url=https://www.upi.com/Entertainment_News/TV/2023/05/18/Futurama-Hulu-July-24/7491684433854/ |work=UPI}}</ref>

On November 2, 2023, Hulu renewed the series for tenth and eleventh production seasons;<ref name="season-13-14-renewal"/> a total of 20 episodes were ordered for the new seasons, which will air from 2025 to 2026.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Rice |first=Lynette |date=November 2, 2023 |title='Futurama' Renewed for Two More Seasons by Hulu |url=https://deadline.com/2023/11/futurama-renewed-two-more-seasons-hulu-1235590020/ |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=Deadline}}</ref><ref name="2026renewal">{{cite web |last=Massoto |first=Erick |date= November 2, 2023 |title='Futurama' Renewed for Two More Seasons |url=https://collider.com/futurama-season-13-14-renewed/ |access-date=April 1, 2024 |work=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]}}</ref> All of season ten was released on Hulu on September 15, 2025,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://deadline.com/2025/07/futurama-season-13-return-all-episodes-1236463638/|title='Futurama': All 10 Episodes of Season 13 To Drop In September|first=Lynette|last=Rice|publisher=Deadline Hollywood|date=July 21, 2025|accessdate=August 1, 2025}}</ref> while [[FXX]] began airing new episodes weekly the same day.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2025/tv/news/futurama-season-13-drop-at-once-hulu-weekly-premiere-date-1236465637/|title=Hulu Switches 'Futurama' Season 13 From Weekly to Binge Release; Shares Premiere Date and First Look Photos (EXCLUSIVE)|website=Variety|date=July 21, 2025|last=Schneider|first=Michael}}</ref> The eleventh season premiered on August 3, 2026.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/futurama-season-14-release-schedule/|title=Futurama season 14 release schedule: When are new episodes out?|first=Morgan|last=Cormack|work=Radio Times|date=August 3, 2026|accessdate=August 3, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.syracuse.com/tv/2026/08/futurama-season-14-premieres-today-how-to-watch-for-free-on-hulu.html|title='Futurama' Season 14 premieres today: How to watch for free on Hulu|first=Madison|last=Kemeny|website=syracuse.com|date=August 2, 2026|accessdate=August 3, 2026}}</ref>

On July 25, 2026, Matt Groening, the series’ executive producers and cast announced during a panel discussion at the 2026 [[San Diego Comic-Con]] that Hulu had ordered 3 new extended-length specials, ahead of the season eleven premiere. Hulu would confirm this as well. The first of these new specials, set to have a Christmas theme, will premiere in 2027.<ref name="sp1">{{Cite web |last=Campione |first=Katie |date=2026-07-25 |title='Futurama' Gets 3 Extended Special Episodes; Season 14 Trailer Debuts |url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/futurama-new-extended-episodes-season-14-trailer-1237003526/ |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="sp2">{{Cite web |last=Schneider |first=Michael |date=2026-07-25 |title='Futurama' to Release Three New Supersized Specials, Including a Christmas Episode, Starting Next Year on Hulu |url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/futurama-three-new-supersized-specials-hulu-comic-con-1236821009/ |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

The show received critical acclaim. The first season holds an 82% approval rating at [[review aggregator]] site [[Rotten Tomatoes]], based on 32 reviews, an average rating of 8.75/10. The critical consensus reads, "Good news, everyone! ''Futurama'' is an inventive, funny, and sometimes affecting look at the world of tomorrow." Season 5 holds a rating of 100%, based on seven reviews, and an average score of 8.67/10. Season 6 has an approval rating of 100%, based on 16 reviews, and the average rating is 8.31/10. The website's critical consensus states, "Good news everyone! ''Futurama'' is as funny and endearing as ever in its sixth season." The next season received a rating of 92%, and an 8.24/10 average score based on 12 reviews. The critics consensus reads, "''Futurama'' makes the most of its second life with biting social satire, kooky sci-fi scenarios, and a stirringly sweet series finale."<ref name="RT">{{Cite web |title=Futurama |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/futurama/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190504190558/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/futurama |archive-date=May 4, 2019 |access-date=November 27, 2018 |publisher=[[Rotten Tomatoes]]}}</ref> For the eighth season,{{efn|group name=n|Rotten Tomatoes uses FOX's broadcast order, listing the show as eleven seasons; the eighth season is labeled "season 11", but reviews of previous seasons are included following the production order.}} 86% of 29 reviews are positive, while the consensus states, "Shut up and take our money!".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Futurama: Season 11 {{!}} Rotten Tomatoes |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/futurama/s11 |access-date=2026-03-05 |website=www.rottentomatoes.com |language=en}}</ref> In 2013, [[TV Guide]] ranked ''Futurama'' on its list of the "60 Greatest TV Cartoons of All Time".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sands |first=Rich |date=September 24, 2013 |title=TV Guide Magazine's 60 Greatest Cartoons of All Time |url=https://www.tvguide.com/news/greatest-cartoons-tv-guide-magazine-1071203.aspx |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180710095501/https://www.tvguide.com/news/greatest-cartoons-tv-guide-magazine-1071203/ |archive-date=July 10, 2018 |access-date=July 14, 2014 |website=TVGuide.com}}</ref>

''Futurama''{{'}}s 7:00&nbsp;p.m. Sunday time slot caused the show to often be pre-empted by sports and usually have a later-than-average season premiere. It also allowed the writers and animators to get ahead of the broadcast schedule so that episodes intended for one season were not aired until the following season. By the beginning of the fourth broadcast season, all the episodes to be aired that season had already been completed and writers were working at least a year in advance.<ref name="SciFiWeekly2">{{Cite web |date=December 17, 2001 |title=David X. Cohen boards the Planet Express to find meaning in Futurama |url=http://www.scifi.com/sfw/interviews/sfw7897.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080610080245/http://www.scifi.com/sfw/interviews/sfw7897.html |archive-date=June 10, 2008 |access-date=June 3, 2008 |publisher=Sci Fi Weekly}}</ref>

When ''Futurama'' debuted in the Fox Sunday night lineup at 8:30&nbsp;p.m. between ''The Simpsons'' and ''[[The X-Files]]'' on March 28, 1999, it managed 19&nbsp;million viewers, tying for 11th overall in that week's [[Nielsen ratings]].<ref name="Bauder">{{Cite news |last=Bauder |first=David |date=April 1, 1999 |title=New animated show 'Futurama' may be a score for Fox |publisher=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]] |url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=MWSB&p_theme=mwsb&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EB82C9405B7CAA1&p_field_direct-0=document_id |url-status=live |access-date=June 3, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110609012934/http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=MWSB&p_theme=mwsb&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EB82C9405B7CAA1&p_field_direct-0=document_id |archive-date=June 9, 2011}}</ref> The following week, airing at the same time, ''Futurama'' drew 14.2&nbsp;million viewers. The third episode, the first airing on Tuesday, drew 8.85&nbsp;million viewers.<ref name="DailyTV">{{Cite web |date=April 1999 |title=Groening's Gripe |url=http://www.frcr.com/library/dailytv1.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000824051808/http://www.frcr.com/library/dailytv1.html |archive-date=August 24, 2000 |access-date=June 3, 2008}}</ref> Though its ratings were well below ''The Simpsons'', the first season of ''Futurama'' rated higher than competing animated series: ''[[King of the Hill]]'', ''[[Family Guy]]'', ''[[Dilbert (TV series)|Dilbert]]'', ''[[South Park]]'', and ''[[The PJs]]''.<ref name="Sterngold">{{Cite news |last=Sterngold |first=James |date=July 22, 1999 |title=Futurama: Bringing an Alien and a Robot to TV Life |work=The New York Times |url=http://www.frcr.com/library/new_york_times1.html |access-date=June 3, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000824051735/http://www.frcr.com/library/new_york_times1.html |archive-date=August 24, 2000}}</ref>

When ''Futurama'' was effectively canceled in 2003, it had averaged 6.4&nbsp;million viewers for the first half of its fourth broadcast season.<ref name="MLMag">{{Cite web |date=February 14, 2002 |title=Fox puts 'Futurama' order on hold |url=http://www.medialifemagazine.com/news2002/feb02/feb11/4_thurs/news7thursday.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081216141740/http://www.medialifemagazine.com/news2002/feb02/feb11/4_thurs/news7thursday.html |archive-date=December 16, 2008 |access-date=June 3, 2008}}</ref>

In late 2002, [[Cartoon Network]] acquired exclusive cable syndication rights to ''Futurama'' for a reported $10 million (equivalent to ${{inflation|US-GDP|10|2002|r=0|fmt=c}} million in {{inflation/year|US-GDP}}).{{Inflation/fn|US-GDP}}<ref name="APArchiveCN">{{Cite news |date=September 11, 2002 |title=Cartoon Network to Air 'Futurama' |agency=[[Associated Press]] |url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-11097857.html |url-status=usurped |access-date=April 15, 2012 |via=[[HighBeam Research]] |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130523181616/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-11097857.html |location=Dubuque |work=Telegraph - Herald |archive-date=May 23, 2013}}</ref> In January 2003,<ref name="APArchiveCN" /> the network began airing ''Futurama'' episodes as the centerpiece to the expansion of their [[Adult Swim]] cartoon block. Spanish-language ''Futurama'' reruns were broadcast on the [[NBC]]-owned [[Universo (TV channel)|mun2]] cable network from March 3, 2003 to July 9, 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/647593651/|title=March 3, 2003 TV listings|publisher=[[The Miami Herald]]|date=March 2, 2003}}</ref> In October 2005, Comedy Central picked up the cable syndication rights to air ''Futurama''{{'}}s 72-episode run at the start of 2008, following the expiration of Cartoon Network's contract.<ref name="variety">{{Cite news |last=Dempsey, John |date=October 27, 2005 |title="Futurama" in Comedy Central's future via big deal |work=Variety |url=https://variety.com/2005/digital/markets-festivals/animation-central-1117931802/ |url-status=live |access-date=October 27, 2005 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071011195632/http://variety.com/article/VR1117931802.html?categoryid=14&cs=1 |archive-date=October 11, 2007}}</ref> A Comedy Central teaser trailer announced the return of ''Futurama'' March 23, 2008,<ref name="FoxStopProduction">{{Cite web |date=January 19, 2001 |title=Silver screen Simpsons, Futurama facing finish? |url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/cult/news/02021902.shtml |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030419181300/http://www.bbc.co.uk/cult/news/02021902.shtml |archive-date=April 19, 2003 |access-date=June 3, 2008 |website=BBC News}}</ref> which was ''Bender's Big Score'' divided into four episodes followed by the other three movies.

On June 24, 2010, the season 6 premiere, "[[Rebirth (Futurama)|Rebirth]]", drew 2.92 million viewers in the 10:00&nbsp;p.m. time slot on Comedy Central.<ref name="Gorman">{{Cite web |last=Gorman |first=Bill |date=June 25, 2010 |title=UPDATED Thursday Cable Ratings: Futurama Returns Strong; Plus Burn Notice, Royal Pains, NBA Draft & More |url=http://tvbythenumbers.com/2010/06/25/thursday-cable-ratings-futurama-returns-strong/55378 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100627171359/http://tvbythenumbers.com/2010/06/25/thursday-cable-ratings-futurama-returns-strong/55378 |archive-date=June 27, 2010 |access-date=June 26, 2010}}</ref> The second episode of the sixth season, "[[In-A-Gadda-Da-Leela]]", aired at 10:30&nbsp;p.m., immediately following the season premiere. "In-A-Gadda-Da-Leela" drew 2.78 million viewers.<ref name="Gorman" /> This was the series' premiere on the network, with original episodes—the fifth season had previously aired on the network, but it had originally been released in the form of the four direct-to-video films.

[[Nielsen Media Research]], which records viewership on certain American television screens, reported that ''Futurama'' accumulated 14.5 billion minutes of viewing across linear television and streaming platforms between September 22, 2025, and September 20, 2026, ranking as the fifteenth most-watched animated series during that period.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 2026 |title=Drawn to Watch: Animation’s Hit Makers |url=https://www.nielsen.com/insights/2026/drawn-to-watch-animations-hit-makers/ |access-date=2026-11-06 |website=[[Nielsen Media Research]] |publisher=[[Nielsen Holdings]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2026-10-27 |title=Nielsen Animation Day 2026 Reports Highlights Key Toon TV & Streaming Trends |url=https://www.animationmagazine.net/2026/10/nielsen-animation-day-2026-reports-highlights-key-toon-tv-streaming-trends/ |access-date=2026-11-06 |website=[[Animation Magazine]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Other honors===
[[File:Futurama Nixon At Library.jpg|thumb|An illustration of the character [[Cultural depictions of Richard Nixon|Richard Nixon, President of Earth]], on display at the [[Richard Nixon Presidential Library and Museum]]]]
* In January 2009, [[IGN]] named ''Futurama'' as the eighth best in the "Top 100 Animated TV Series".<ref name="IGN100">{{Cite web |date=January 2009 |title=Top 100 Animated TV Series |url=http://tv.ign.com/top-100-animated-tv-series/8.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100327195215/http://tv.ign.com/top-100-animated-tv-series/8.html |archive-date=March 27, 2010 |access-date=March 22, 2010 |publisher=IGN}}</ref>
* At the 2010 [[San Diego Comic-Con]], [[Guinness World Records]] presented ''Futurama'' with the record for "Current Most Critically Acclaimed Animated Series".<ref name="Cordova">{{Cite web |last=Cordova |first=Gonzalo |date=July 24, 2010 |title=Comedy Central at Comic-Con: Day Three, Futurama Panel |url=http://ccinsider.comedycentral.com/2010/07/24/comedy-central-at-comic-con-day-three-futurama-panel/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120710201045/http://ccinsider.comedycentral.com/2010/07/24/comedy-central-at-comic-con-day-three-futurama-panel/ |archive-date=July 10, 2012 |access-date=August 1, 2010 |website=Comedy Central Insider |publisher=[[Comedy Central]]}}</ref>
* In 2020, ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' ranked it as the thirty-ninth best science fiction television show ever.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last1=Adams |first1=Sam |last2=Collins |first2=Sean T. |last3=Fear |first3=David |last4=Murray |first4=Noel |last5=Scherer |first5=Jenna |last6=Tobias |first6=Scott |date=March 12, 2020 |title=50 Best Science Fiction TV Shows of All Time |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/tv/tv-lists/best-science-fiction-tv-shows-of-all-time-65434/ |url-status=live |access-date=June 11, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160527141422/http://www.rollingstone.com/tv/lists/40-best-science-fiction-tv-shows-20160526 |archive-date=May 27, 2016}}</ref>

==Other media==
===Comic books===
{{Main|Futurama Comics|l1 = ''Futurama Comics''}}

First started in November 2000 and lasting until July 2018, ''Futurama Comics'' is a comic book series published by [[Bongo Comics Group|Bongo Comics]] based in the ''Futurama'' universe.<ref name="comics">{{Cite news |date=November 19, 2000 |title=Groening launches 'Futurama Comics' |url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=NewsLibrary&p_multi=CSGB&d_place=CSGB&p_theme=newslibrary2&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0F34B832C954DA1A&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM |url-status=dead |access-date=July 16, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110609013008/http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=NewsLibrary&p_multi=CSGB&d_place=CSGB&p_theme=newslibrary2&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0F34B832C954DA1A&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM |archive-date=June 9, 2011}}</ref> While originally published only in the US, a UK, German and Australian version of the series is also available.<ref>Press release (September 25, 2002) [http://www.gotfuturama.com/Information/Articles/titan.shtml Do you want Fry with that?] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927172507/http://www.gotfuturama.com/Information/Articles/titan.shtml |date=September 27, 2007}} ''Titan Publishing''. Retrieved from gotfuturama on March 4, 2007</ref> In addition, three issues were published in Norway. Other than a different running order and presentation, the stories are the same in all versions. While the comics focus on the same characters in the ''Futurama'' [[fictional universe]], the comics may not be [[canon (fiction)|canonical]] as the events portrayed within them do not necessarily have any effect upon the continuity of the show.

Like the TV series, each comic (except US comic #20) has a caption at the top of the cover. For example: "Made In The USA! (Printed in Canada)". Some of the UK and Australian comics have different captions on the top of their comics (for example, the Australian version of #20 says "A 21st Century Comic Book" across the cover, while the US version does not have a caption on that issue). All series contain a letters page, artwork from readers, and previews of other upcoming Bongo comics.

Its final issue was on July 18, 2018, three months before Bongo Comics would shut down.<ref>{{cite news|last=Boothby|first=Ian|title=Just announced in San Diego|url=https://twitter.com/IanBoothby/status/1021860190012882944|access-date=25 July 2018|website=Twitter|date=25 July 2018}}</ref>

===Films===
{{see also|Futurama season 5|l1=''Futurama'' season 5}}
When Comedy Central began negotiating for the rights to air ''Futurama'' reruns, Fox suggested that there was a possibility of also creating new episodes. Negotiations were already underway with the possibility of creating two or three [[Direct-to-video|direct-to-DVD]] films. When Comedy Central committed to sixteen new episodes, it was decided that four films would be produced.<ref name="Katz" /> On April 26, 2006, Groening noted in an interview that co-creator David X. Cohen and numerous writers from the original series would be returning to work on the movies.<ref name="DVDMovieAnnounced">{{Cite web |last=Rabin, Nathan |date=April 26, 2006 |title=Matt Groening |url=https://www.avclub.com/matt-groening-1798209542 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090119014837/http://www.avclub.com/articles/matt-groening,13984/ |archive-date=January 19, 2009 |access-date=June 3, 2008 |publisher=[[The A.V. Club]]}}</ref> All the original voice actors participated. In February 2007, Groening explained the format of the new stories: "[The crew is] writing them as movies and then we're going to chop them up, reconfigure them, write new material and try to make them work as separate episodes."<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 26, 2007 |title=Rhymes with Raining |url=http://www.craveonline.com/articles/filmtv/04647510/rhymes_with_raining.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090215100510/http://www.craveonline.com/articles/filmtv/04647510/rhymes_with_raining.html |archive-date=February 15, 2009 |access-date=March 25, 2007 |website=Crave Online}}</ref>

The first film, ''[[Futurama: Bender's Big Score|Bender's Big Score]]'', was written by Ken Keeler and Cohen, and includes return appearances by the [[Nibblonian]]s, Seymour, Barbados Slim, [[Robot Santa]], [[Godfellas|the "God" space entity]], [[List of recurring Futurama characters#Al Gore|Al Gore]], and Zapp Brannigan.<ref name="AIC-BendersBigScore">{{Cite web |title=Ain't It Cool News: "Ben Sinister Has Read The New FUTURAMA 'Movie'!!" |url=https://www.aintitcool.com/display.cgi?id=24076 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060806011505/http://www.aintitcool.com/display.cgi?id=24076 |archive-date=August 6, 2006 |access-date=June 3, 2008}}</ref> It was animated in widescreen and was released on standard DVD on November 27, 2007, with a possible [[Blu-ray Disc]] release to follow.<ref name="Simpsons and Futurama in HD">(April 5, 2008). {{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20080723220501/http://www.hdtvtotal.com/module-pagesetter-viewpub-tid-1-pid-1146.html Tales of Interest: The Simpsons and Futurama in high-definition]}}. HDTVTotal.com.</ref> A release on [[HD DVD]] was rumored but later officially denied. ''Futurama: Bender's Big Score'' was the first DVD release for which 20th Century Fox implemented measures intended to reduce the total carbon footprint of the production, manufacturing, and distribution processes. Where it was not possible to completely eliminate carbon, output [[carbon offset]]s were used, thus making the complete process [[carbon neutrality|carbon neutral]].<ref name="2Snaps">{{Cite web |date=November 14, 2007 |title="Futurama" Feature Length Movie DVD Specs |url=http://www.2snaps.tv/9812689 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080406004938/http://www.2snaps.tv/9812689 |archive-date=April 6, 2008 |access-date=June 3, 2008}}</ref>

The second movie, ''[[Futurama: The Beast with a Billion Backs|The Beast with a Billion Backs]]'', was released on June 24, 2008. The third movie, ''[[Futurama: Bender's Game|Bender's Game]]'', was released on DVD and Blu-ray Disc<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hornig |first=Andreas |date=July 28, 2008 |title=Futurama's third direct-to-disc movie "Bender's Game" on Blu-ray |url=http://www.hdtvtotal.com/module-pagesetter-viewpub-tid-1-pid-1210.html |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130613075844/http://www.hdtvtotal.com/module-pagesetter-viewpub-tid-1-pid-1210.html |archive-date=June 13, 2013 |access-date=August 10, 2008 |publisher=HDTVTotal.com}}</ref> on November 3, 2008, in the UK, November 4, 2008, in the US, and December 10, 2008, in Australia. The fourth movie, ''[[Futurama: Into the Wild Green Yonder|Into the Wild Green Yonder]]'', was released on DVD and Blu-ray Disc on February 24, 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Into the Wild Green Yonder at Blu-ray.com |url=http://www.blu-ray.com/movies/movies.php?id=1889 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120722103911/http://www.blu-ray.com/movies/Futurama-Into-The-Wild-Green-Yonder-Blu-ray/1889/ |archive-date=July 22, 2012 |access-date=February 23, 2009 |publisher=Blu-ray.com}}</ref>

Following the series' revival, the show's executive producer [[Claudia Katz]] had announced more upcoming movies for [[Hulu]] while also hinting at a theatrical release.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Philips|first=TC|date=September 8, 2023|title=Futurama EP Teases More Movies After Season 11 Revival|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/futurama-movies-series-return-exclusive-newsupdate/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230909025543/https://screenrant.com/futurama-season-11-12-movies-future-producer-response/|archive-date=September 9, 2023|access-date=January 11, 2024|publisher=ScreenRant}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=A Futurama Movie Could Be In The Cards At Hulu|last=Seibold|first=Witney|date=September 16, 2023|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1395519/futurama-hulu-possible-movie/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231102200639/https://www.slashfilm.com/1395519/futurama-hulu-possible-movie/|archive-date=November 2, 2023|access-date=February 14, 2024|publisher=SlashFilm}}</ref>

===Video games===
{{see also|Futurama (video game)|l1=''Futurama'' (video game)|Futurama: Worlds of Tomorrow|l2=''Futurama: Worlds of Tomorrow''}}
On September 15, 2000, Unique Development Studios acquired the license to develop a ''Futurama'' video game for consoles and handheld systems. [[Fox Interactive]] signed on to publish the game.<ref name="VideoGame1">{{Cite web |title=Futurama Finds a Developer |url=http://www.gamespot.com/news/2628824.html?q=Futurama |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930064405/http://www.gamespot.com/news/2628824.html?q=Futurama |archive-date=September 30, 2007 |access-date=July 25, 2006}}</ref> [[Sierra Entertainment]] later became the game's publisher, and it was released on August 14, 2003.<ref name="VideoGame2">{{Cite web |title=Sierra to bring Futurama game to the US |url=http://www.gamespot.com/news/6025618.html?q=Futurama |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930161529/http://www.gamespot.com/news/6025618.html?q=Futurama |archive-date=September 30, 2007 |access-date=June 3, 2008}}</ref> Versions are available for [[PlayStation 2]] and [[Xbox (console)|Xbox]], both of which use [[Cel shading|cel-shading]] technology. However, the game was subsequently canceled on the [[GameCube]] and [[Game Boy Advance]] in North America and Europe.

In 2012, an app inspired by the head in a jar gag was launched by Matt Groening.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 11, 2012 |title=Groening Launches 'Futurama' Head-in-a-Jar App |url=https://www.animationmagazine.net/licensing/groening-launches-futurama-head-in-a-jar-app/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211007172850/https://www.animationmagazine.net/licensing/groening-launches-futurama-head-in-a-jar-app/ |archive-date=October 7, 2021 |access-date=October 7, 2021}}</ref>

In September 2016, ''Futurama'' characters and content would be playable in a crossover [[free-to-play]] digital collectable card video game ''[[Animation Throwdown: The Quest for Cards]]'', which also contained characters and content from other [[20th Television Animation]] properties; particularly ''[[Family Guy]]'', ''[[American Dad!]]'', ''[[King of the Hill]]'', ''[[Bob's Burgers]]'', and ''[[Archer (2009 TV series)|Archer]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.alistdaily.com/media/gamestop-exec-fox-animated-tv-show-digital-card-game/ |title=GameStop Exec Discusses Fox Animated TV Show Digital Card Game |work=A.List |last=Gaudiosi |first=John |date=June 27, 2016 |access-date=May 14, 2023}}</ref> The game was released on September 27, 2016 and is available for [[Android (operating system)|Android]], [[iOS]], [[Steam (service)|Steam]], [[Kongregate#Kartridge|Kartridge]]<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Animation Throwdown|url=https://www.kartridge.com/games/Throwdown/animation-throwdown|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201028210602/https://www.kartridge.com/games/Throwdown/animation-throwdown|archive-date=2020-10-28|access-date=2020-10-25|website=www.kartridge.com}}</ref> and on the web via the game's developer [[Kongregate]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kongregate.com/games/Throwdown/animation-throwdown|title=Animation Throwdown|website=Kongregate}}</ref>

Licensing for mobile games were done in 2016 with ''Futurama: Game of Drones'' and in 2017 with ''[[Futurama: Worlds of Tomorrow]]'', which was released for [[Android (operating system)|Android]] and [[iOS]] in 2017.<ref>[https://news.cision.com/wooga/r/:~:text=In%20FUTURAMA:%20Game%20of%20Drones,control%20of%20the%20evil%20MomCo] {{dead link|date=January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The 'Futurama' crew returns today in a new mobile game |date=June 29, 2017 |url=https://www.engadget.com/2017/06/29/futurama-worlds-of-tomorrow-available/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170629174451/https://www.engadget.com/2017/06/29/futurama-worlds-of-tomorrow-available/ |archive-date=June 29, 2017 |access-date=June 29, 2017}}</ref>

On July 25, 2023, ''[[Fortnite]]'' released an update that included theme content centered on the show ''Futurama'', including purchasable outfits. These outfits include Bender Bending Rodríguez, Philip J. Fry, and Turanga Leela, as well as other themed accessories. The weapon "Bender's Shiny Metal Raygun" has also been included in the game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 26, 2023 |title=Fortnite Battle Royale V25.20 Update: Futurama Bender, Fry, and Leela Outfits Arrive! |url=https://www.fortnite.com/news/fortnite-battle-royale-v25-20-update-futurama-bender-fry-and-leela-outfits-arrive |access-date=July 26, 2023 |website=Fortnite {{!}} Create, Play & Battle With Friends for Free - Fortnite |publisher=Epic Games}}</ref>
